title: JAIMS Research Article (Clinical & Formulation Study)
subtitle: Peer-Reviewed Transdermal Drug Delivery Engineering, Permeation & Human Clinical Trial
institution: Journal of Ayurveda and Integrated Medical Sciences (JAIMS)
overview: Published in the Journal of Ayurveda and Integrated Medical Sciences (JAIMS 2026; 11(7): 107–117), this peer-reviewed study details the engineering, drug release performance, and clinical evaluation of the transdermal patch formulation.

keyOutcomes.label: Clinical Relief Speed
keyOutcomes.description: 96% of participants reported noticeable relief from menstrual cramps within 30 minutes.

keyOutcomes.label: Cumulative Drug Release
keyOutcomes.description: Controlled biphasic permeation profile achieving 91.23% release over 12+ continuous hours.

keyOutcomes.label: Gastro-Sparing Advantage
keyOutcomes.description: Bypasses hepatic first-pass and gastric mucosa, presenting an optimal alternative to oral NSAIDs.

clinicalDetails.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and Integrated Medical Sciences (JAIMS)
clinicalDetails.onsetSpeed: Noticeable relief within 30 minutes in 96% of cohort
clinicalDetails.cumulativeRelease: 91.23% over 12 hours via ex-vivo skin permeation testing
clinicalDetails.advantage: Provides an effective, non-invasive, gastro-sparing alternative to conventional oral NSAIDs (such as naproxen sodium) by bypassing systemic GI absorption.
